rules_text:
Rules summary Contents 1 Overview 2 Solo Play 3 Multiplayer 4 Score Overview The Quest: Defeat a deck of foes with your 5 dice in this yahtzee/dice manipulation D&D inspired adventure. Once defeated, you gain the cards' special dice modification abilities. You must use them judiciously, as your final score is the number of cards captured that you DIDN'T use...but if you fail to defeat a monster each turn, you lose the game. Solo Play Play the following phases: [1] The quest area is filled or completed with 5 creature cards. [2] Roll 5d6 - If you roll a combination matching the dice shown at the bottom of a card, you can declare that you beat it and put it in your army area. If you can beat more than one card, choose one. [3] Free reroll - Once per turn you can try to get better dice results by rerolling any number of dice, keeping the new results. Note that the very first roll of a game you get 2 free rerolls. [4] Modify roll - You can use any number of cards in your army to modify your dice roll. Discard each army card after you use it. The effect of an army card is depicted by the symbol in its upper right corner: ​ add 1 to a die [max is ​ ]; ​ subtract 1 from a die [min is ​ ]; ​ add or subtract 1 to a die [as above]; ​ reroll any number of dice; keep results; ​ mirror a die to its opposite: ​ to ​ , ​ to ​ , ​ to ​ , ​ to ​ , etc. [5] Check for game end conditions - If you beat a card and there are more monster cards to beat, start over from phase [1]. If you didn't defeat a monster, you lose the game. If the deck AND the quest area have no cards left, you won. Your SCORE is the number of cards left in your army. Dice Requirement Examples: Cards showing a value of dice like, ​ ​ are beaten by a roll of those same numbers in at least that quantity, so a roll of ​ ​ ​ ​ ​ would succeed because it contains the required pair of 2s. if you roll had rolled ​ ​ ​ ​ ​ , you would still succeed because you had rolled the required pair of 2s ​ and ​ symbols represent any number, making the requirement only that you have a certain number of a single value. For example: ​ ​ can be beaten by any pair of numbers ​ ​ ​ can be beaten by any value three of a kind, and so on. If a card has both Suns and Moons, they may represent the same or different numbers . ​ ​ ​ ​ would require two pairs of numbers OR a four of a kind. ​ ​ ​ ​ ​ would require a pair of one value and a three of a kind of another OR a five of a kind. Multiplayer Players take turns clockwise, using the same rules of solo play. The quest area is shared by all the players, while army tableaus are private. Whether or not a player beats a monster card during their turn, the game continues until there are no cards left in the deck and quest area. Compare the sum of army plus discarded cards of each player: the highest score wins. In case of a tie, the player with the most unused army cards wins. Score The maximum attainable score is 42, although it's unlikely to beat all the cards without using any of them. A score over 20 is good, and reaching 30 is great.

[Rating: 2/10] Just luck rolling dice, with modifiers that come from cards previously taken with dice.  That's not a runaway leader, but almost it is. You gain 5 cards before your opponent starts taking his first one? Ok, you already know you will win by 5 points, for example 23-18.

[Rating: 2/10] Played 3 on BGA. First 2 ended in the 2nd round, the last one in the 1st round. I really just tried it because it was the "treasure" in one of the boxes of the 2025 Summer Calendar on BGA.

[Rating: 2/10] I was intrigued by the concept, but in play I just did not find it engaging. It felt too simple and too long. I would not be averse to trying something similar but with more substance.

[Rating: 2/10] [i]Slay the dragon with five of a kind.[/i] Played in: [url=https://boardgamegeek.com/geeklist/350958/item/12046525][u]2025[/u][/url]

[Rating: 2/10] I had a few solo plays on BGA. It is luck dependent. A sort of Yahtzee with cards. If you ask me, Yahtzee is a better game.  This one had some potential, but the design stoped a the very basic options of roll then score ore roll, modify (If you can) then score. The cards must have been more developed, from a design point (more options, more VPs scales, additional end game trigger and other stuff like this to make it a board game). I don't give low scores in BGG, but the fact that this game was published in 2022 has no excuse. The game industry has evolved. Dear designers, try more, please. I l

[Rating: 2/10] It depends heavily on luck. — There are some interesting ideas, but I got the impression that there was a certain amount of laziness during development: whoever tested the game was either very lucky or didn’t mind games ending in the first or second round. I’ve lost several games where, as early as the first round, I found myself facing 4 or more monsters that required 4 or 5 dice. Perhaps the ability to choose monsters from 2 different sets to create a more balanced battle line could make the game more fun.

[Rating: 3/10] Solo Yahtzee with perhaps slightly more luck because of a random pile of cards. Not a game for me.

[Rating: 3/10] There's really no substance here. Player is just rolling dice trying to get poker hands. There are ways to mitigate dice but the game is just too simple and the dice rolling is more luck based than I would like.
